assumptions.obligation: The APB Requester is reset together with the bridge. While i_rst_n_core is low, i_apb_psel and i_apb_penable are 0.
A Setup phase (PSEL=1, PENABLE=0) is followed in the next cycle by an Access phase (PSEL=1, PENABLE=1). The Access phase holds PSEL and PENABLE high until o_apb_pready is 1.

PENABLE is high only in an Access phase that follows a Setup phase or continues an Access phase that is not complete. After PREADY the next cycle is idle or a new Setup phase (back-to-back with PSEL held high is allowed), and it is never a direct Access phase.
i_apb_paddr, i_apb_pwrite, i_apb_pwdata and i_apb_pstrb stay unchanged from the Setup phase until PREADY.

TL-UL D-channel handshake (REF-005 protocol checked at the ports). When d_valid=1 is not accepted (o_tlul_d_ready=0), the device keeps d_valid high and every D-channel payload field stable in the next cycle.

notes:
I only constrained sequencing and stability. These are deliberately left unconstrained:
(1) Misaligned PADDR and write PSTRB != 4'b1111 stay free. BR-6.2-01/02 call them "must", but the bridge must detect them and answer with PSLVERR (BR-3-24/25, BR-12-xx).
(2) PPROT has no stability constraint. BR-6.3-02 does not list it, and BR-2.3-03 says the bridge ignores it.
(3) i_tlul_a_ready and d_valid timing stay free. This allows any back-pressure, a device that never answers (BR-12-09), a response in the acceptance cycle (BR-6.3-09), and orphan responses (BR-6.3-08, BR-10.1-06, BR-15.1-01). Orphan injection is required, so I did not use the 'one response per accepted request' wording of BR-20-03.
(4) d_opcode, d_source, d_error, d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user can take any value, because wrong opcode, wrong source and d_error are error cases the bridge must report.
(5) d_valid is not forced low during reset, because the asynchronous reset makes it irrelevant.

ENV-05 (the D-channel hold) has a weaker basis than the others. No BR rule states it directly. It comes from the TL-UL valid/ready protocol of REF-005, which is checked at the ports (BR-15.1-02). It only has an effect when o_tlul_d_ready is 0, which normally happens only in the first cycle after reset release.

Reset release is synchronous (BR-7.3-01). Both helper registers are cleared by reset, so all past-based assumptions are inactive in the first cycle after release.
